Q: Running a Class.method() when that module is imported A:

The best way to run code while the class is being defined, is to run that code in the class definition. In the comments you mentioned you want to initialise logging and such. Well, just do this in the class definition:

import logging

class Foo:
    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

class blocks can contain regular code, not just assignment statements.

This logger creation will be run once when the class is being defined, which happens the first time something imports the module this class is defined in.

(Arguably loggers should be module scoped, not class scoped, but I won't try to dissuade you of that here.)

Q: YouTube iframe always overlays the video for ~3 seconds before disappearing A:

This is a very long and thorough question. I managed to get rid of everything except the pause icon. In your code I replaced:

.frame iframe       { width:100%; height:100%; border:0; display:block; }

by:

.frame iframe       { width:300%; height:100%; margin-left: -100%; border:0; }

This makes the iframe wider, and then moves the video back into view. Not perfect, but it is a start. This means you can affect most of the chrome, and probably the pause button as well.

Other people also struggle with the pause button. For instance this attempt.

To be honest, I don't think Youtube will be happy with this, it is their video-stream after all. I scanned their terms-of-service but couldn't find anything applicable.

Q: What should I learn first to start a career in AI and Machine Learning? A:

If you are a beginner and want to start a career in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, I recommend learning the topics in a structured order.

First, learn Python programming, especially functions, loops, object-oriented programming, and basic data structures. Then learn important Python libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Scikit-learn.

After that, focus on data preprocessing, exploratory data analysis (EDA), supervised and unsupervised learning, regression, classification, clustering, and model evaluation. Once you understand the basics of Machine Learning, you can move on to Deep Learning, neural networks, TensorFlow/PyTorch, and Generative AI.

The best way to learn is by building practical projects, such as a student marks prediction system, house price prediction, spam detection, recommendation system, or image classification project.

Q: How many backslashes are needed to escape characters in grep? A:

The lowercase -e option is used to express multiple search operations. The alternation is implied:

$ echo abcdef | grep -e 'def' -e'zzz'
abcdef
$ echo abczzz | grep -e 'def' -e'zzz'
abczzz

Alternatively, you can use the upper -E option for extended regular expression notation:

$ echo abcdef | grep -E 'def|zzz'
abcdef

I believe this solves you problem directly (either using -e for alternation or -E for extended regex notation). Hope this helps :-)

FWIW, the issue with the backslashes is that | has special meaning to bash and needs to be escaped unless it is in single quotes. Here is a resource on quoting and escaping rules and the common pitfalls: https://web.archive.org/web/20230323230844/https://wiki.bash-hackers.org/syntax/quoting

Q: Why doesn't template_matching delete the previous ROI A:

Here is an example of how to do that for one of your templates in Python OpenCV.

The main idea is to used masked template matching to avoid too close matches and avoid mismatches to other areas in the image.

(Note: I think your posted template might be larger than it should so I cropped a new template from your image to be sure it was of a matching size)

  • Read the image

  • Read the template

  • Threshld the template by any means that works

  • Get the largest contour

  • Draw the contour as white filled on a black background as the mask

  • Do the template matching using TM_SQDIFF as the method

  • In a loop over a number larger than the expected number of matches, get the minvalue, max value, min location and max location of each match. Then use a threshold test to keep only matches below the threshold.

  • For each good match, draw a rectangle about the match in a copy of the input image and draw a max value color over the current correlation image of size approximately a quarter of the dimensions of the template image, so that the next match is not too close to the previous one

  • Save the results

Input:

Template image:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read game image
img = cv2.imread('curcuit_board.jpg')

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read game image
img = cv2.imread('circuit2_board.jpg')

# read template
template = cv2.imread('circuit2_template.png')
hh, ww = template.shape[:2]

# threshold template
low = (85,80,110)
high = (250,180,180)
thresh = cv2.inRange(template, low, high)

# get largest contour
contours = cv2.findContours(thresh, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]
big_contour = max(contours, key=cv2.contourArea)

# Draw white filled contour on black background
mask = np.zeros_like(thresh)
cv2.drawContours(mask,[big_contour], 0, 255, -1)

# set arguments
match_thresh = 900000             # stopping threshold for match value
max_matches = 5                   # stopping threshold for number of matches
match_radius = max(hh,ww)//4       # approx radius of match peaks

# do masked template matching and save correlation image
correlation = cv2.matchTemplate(img, template, cv2.TM_SQDIFF, mask=mask)
corr_max = np.max(correlation)
corr_img1 = (correlation * 255 / corr_max).clip(0,255).astype(np.uint8)

# get locations of all peaks higher than match_thresh for up to num_matches
result = img.copy()
correlation2 = correlation.copy()
for i in range(1, max_matches):
    # get max value and location of max
    min_val, max_val, min_loc, max_loc = cv2.minMaxLoc(correlation2)
    x1 = min_loc[0]
    y1 = min_loc[1]
    x2 = x1 + ww
    y2 = y1 + hh
    loc = str(x1) + "," + str(y1)
    #print("match number:", i, "match value:", min_val, "match x,y:", loc)
    if min_val < match_thresh:
        print("match number:", i, "match value:", min_val, "match x,y:", loc)
        # draw draw red bounding box to define match location
        cv2.rectangle(result, (x1,y1), (x2,y2), (0,0,255), 2)
        # draw white circle of value max_val over copy of correlation2 
        cv2.circle(correlation2, (x1,y1), match_radius, int(max_val), -1)
        i = i + 1
    else:
        break

corr_img2 = (correlation2 * 255 / corr_max).clip(0,255).astype(np.uint8)

# save results
cv2.imwrite('circuit2_board_template_thresh.png', thresh)
cv2.imwrite('circuit2_board_template_mask.png', mask)
cv2.imwrite('circuit2_board_correlation_original.png', corr_img1)
cv2.imwrite('circuit2_board_correlation_masked.png', corr_img2)
cv2.imwrite('circuit2_board_vs_template_result.png', result)

cv2.imshow('thresh', thresh)
cv2.imshow('mask', mask)
cv2.imshow('result',result)
cv2.waitKey(0)
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
